artists.biography:
Crowded House are a pop rock band formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1985 by lead-vocalist and primary songwriter, New Zealand-born Neil Finn. Other members have included his brother Tim Finn, Australians Paul Hester, Nick Seymour and Peter Jones and Americans Mark Hart and Matt Sherrod.
Crowded House has won several national and international awards. In Australia, the group has won eleven ARIA Awards from 26 nominations, including the inaugural Best New Talent award in 1987. The majority of their ARIAs were awarded for their first two albums, Crowded House and Temple of Low Men. They won eight APRA Awards from eleven nominations and were nominated for The New Zealand Silver Scroll for "Don't Stop Now" in 2007.
"Don't Dream It's Over" was named the seventh best Australian song of all time in 2001.

perplexity.description:
Released in June 1986, Crowded House is the debut studio album by the New Zealand-Australian rock band Crowded House. The album blends melodic rock with jangly guitar textures, introspective lyrics, and strong vocal harmonies, establishing a sound that would become a hallmark of the band’s style. Produced by Mitchell Froom, the record features standout tracks such as “Don’t Dream It’s Over,” “Something So Strong,” and “Mean to Me,” which showcase Neil Finn’s songwriting prowess and the band’s knack for crafting accessible yet emotionally resonant pop-rock songs.

As the first release under Capitol Records, Crowded House marked the beginning of the band’s international career and set the stage for their subsequent success. The album was a commercial hit, reaching number two on the Australian charts and achieving platinum certification in the United States. Critics praised its melodic craftsmanship and emotional depth, with “Don’t Dream It’s Over” becoming an enduring classic. The album’s success helped define Crowded House’s place in the late 1980s rock landscape and remains a foundational work in their discography.
